benchmarks.name: CyberGym-E2E official board — S3 discover + PoC + patch + tests (headline), $10 budget
benchmarks.description: CyberGym-E2E official leaderboard (UC Berkeley RDI, arXiv 2606.04460): 920 real OSS-Fuzz vulnerabilities in 139 C/C++ projects; the agent discovers the bug, writes a PoC that crashes the unpatched build (S1), patches it (S2) without breaking developer tests (S3); S4 (diagnostic) checks the ground-truth vulnerability is the one fixed. Stages are cumulative; S3 is the headline discover-and-patch rate. Patch-only = agent given the ground-truth PoC and crash log. Rows marked † on the board were run on an earlier 615-task set. Agents run with their vendor CLI (Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenHands) and a 90-minute limit; $10-per-task budget runs by the CyberGym-E2E team (comparable set).

benchmarks.name: DeepsecBench (Vercel board, F2 score)
benchmarks.description: Vercel DeepsecBench (launched 2026-07-27; board at vercel.com/ai-gateway/leaderboards/deepsecbench): vulnerability discovery in one undisclosed open-source codebase pinned before a large batch of fixes — 50 entry-point files, golden set of 231 human-judged findings. Score = recall-weighted F2 = 100·5PR/(4P+R); findings outside the golden set are judged real/false and count toward precision only; median of 3 runs. Run with the vendor harness per model (Codex for OpenAI, Claude Code for Anthropic, Pi for others) via deepsec. AA re-implements it on Stirrup as `deepsecbench_aa` (not comparable). Headline F2 score.

benchmarks.name: Vals CyberBench v1.1 (overall accuracy)

PoC track (60 tasks): from source + fuzz target, produce a crashing input (must crash vulnerable build, not the fixed one). Patch track (56 tasks): given PoC + sanitizer report, patch so the PoC no longer crashes and hidden holdout inputs match the maintainer fix. mini-swe-agent harness; provider refusals count as failures. Overall accuracy.
